summary.title: Vim anti-patterns
summary.one_liner: Common habits that slow down Vim users, and the built-in commands that replace them, such as paragraph and character motions, c instead of d+insert, and o/O for opening lines.
keywords: vim t and f character motion
vim star search word under cursor
how to be faster in vim
takeaways: Use paragraph ({ and }) and screenful (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+B) motions instead of holding j or k.
Use t/f/T/F character motions and search-based motions instead of stepping one character at a time.
Use c instead of d followed by i, and o/O or I/A instead of entering insert mode separately, so operations stay repeatable with '.'.
Stay in normal mode to move around, keep hands on the home row, and use Ctrl+[ instead of Escape; the page also suggests optional remaps such as disabling arrow keys or mapping jj to Escape.
Repeat the last command, search, substitution or macro with @:, n, &, g& or @@ instead of retyping them.
summary.summary: The article lists common Vim habits that waste time, such as moving one line or one character at a time, deleting and then entering insert mode, using arrow keys, and pressing Escape. For each, it gives the more efficient built-in alternative, with short examples and a few optional key mappings (disabling arrow keys, mapping jj to Escape). It also covers repeat commands like @:, &, and @@. The author states that these techniques need no plugins or substantial remapping.
